sources: IDF + Shin Bet joint statement (Friday night); Benjamin Netanyahu (Hebron visit, Friday); Walla (via Jerusalem Post); WAFA; Basma Radio checkpoint monitor; AP scene reporting (via Arab News)
fault_line: Security operation after soldiers are killed, or collective punishment of a whole city days before an election?

sections.what_happened: Beyond the Hebron closures already recorded (all gates impassable by car, dozens evacuated): parallel operations are under way in Jenin and Nablus to locate weapons and make arrests, plus Kafr Aqab in east Jerusalem and Tamun (Walla via JPost). Netanyahu, at Hebron on Friday: 'We will first act to destroy this place and change it completely... We are going to implement the successful and offensive model that we used in the refugee camps... We will clear out the residents, go house to house, take out the weapons and all the infrastructure of terror.' The operation is expected to last several days, with residents exiting only through three designated points after questioning. Hamas praised the Friday attack as a 'natural and legitimate response' without claiming responsibility. Context on record: the attack killed 2 IDF soldiers (Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman, Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem) and wounded 3 others; Palestinian health ministry data cited by AFP counts 1,113 Palestinians killed in the West Bank since Oct 2023.
sections.what_verified: IDF/Shin Bet statement + JPost/Walla + AP scene reporting + WAFA
sections.what_disputed: WAFA/AP scene reporting (evacuations, gate closures, a child blocked from a cancer-related appointment) contradicts any 'surgical only' framing; the IDF did not respond to questions about Saturday's evacuations (AP). The 'refugee-camp model' comparison is Netanyahu's characterisation, not an operational document.
sections.why_matters: Do not report Hebron as a single-city raid: it is now a West Bank-wide operation with a stated doctrine -- the refugee-camp model imported to Hebron, with residents cleared house to house. Lead with the AP gate scene (a child stopped en route to a hospital), then Netanyahu's own words.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261024-1300-03 (Hebron operation, day 2) -- parallel operations in Jenin, Nablus and east Jerusalem; Netanyahu: 'destroy this place and change it completely', house-to-house clearances on the refugee-camp model

totw_analysis: Our read: Do not report Hebron as a single-city raid: it is now a West Bank-wide operation with a stated doctrine -- the refugee-camp model imported to Hebron, with residents cleared house to house. Lead with the AP gate scene (a child stopped en route to a hospital), then Netanyahu's own words. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Security operation after soldiers are killed, or collective punishment of a whole city days before an election?
